'''André Joyal''' ({{IPA|fr|ʒwajal|lang}}; born 1943) is a professor of mathematics at the [[Université du Québec à Montréal]] who works on [[category theory]]. He was a member of the School of Mathematics at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 2013,<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/jandre Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars]</ref> where he was invited to join the ''Special Year on Univalent Foundations of Mathematics''.<ref>[https://www.math.ias.edu/sp/univalent IAS school of mathematics:  Univalent Foundations of Mathematics]</ref>

== Research ==

He discovered [[Kripke–Joyal semantics]],<ref>Robert Goldblatt, A Kripke-Joyal semantics for noncommutative logic in quantales; Advances in Modal Logic 6, 209—225, Coll. Publ., London, 2006; {{MR|2396933 }}</ref> the theory of [[combinatorial species]] and with [[Myles Tierney]] a generalization of the [[Galois theory]] of [[Alexander Grothendieck]]<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1090/MEMO/0309|title=An extension of the Galois theory of Grothendieck |year=1984 |last1=Joyal |first1=André |last2=Tierney |first2=Myles |journal=[[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=51 |issue=309 |doi-access=free }}</ref> in the setup of locales. Most of his research is in some way related to [[category theory]], [[higher category theory]] and their applications. He did some work on [[quasi-category|quasi-categories]], after their invention by [[Michael Boardman]] and Rainer Vogt, in particular conjecturing<ref>A. Joyal, A letter to Grothendieck, April 1983 (contains a Quillen model structure on simplicial presheaves)</ref>  and proving the existence of a [[Daniel Quillen|Quillen]] [[Model category|model structure]] on the category of [[simplicial set]]s whose weak equivalences generalize both equivalence of categories and [[Kan equivalence]] of spaces, which is now known as [[Joyal model structure]]. He co-authored the book "Algebraic Set Theory" with [[Ieke Moerdijk]] and recently started a web-based expositional project Joyal's CatLab <ref>[https://ncatlab.org/joyalscatlab/published Joyal's CatLab]</ref> on categorical mathematics.

== Personal life ==
Joyal was born in [[Drummondville]] (formerly Saint-Majorique). He has three children and lives in [[Montreal]].{{cn|date=May 2025}}
